Q: AWS SSM Session Manager and Nat Gatway A:

If you don't want to pay for the NAT or NAT64 gateways, IPv4 addresses or VPC endpoints (private link) for AWS API access and SSM public endpoints, you can now use IPv6.

I was able to make this work for an instance with no public IPv4 access or NAT gateway. You might need to update route tables to remove IPv4 default routes to NAT or Internet gateway.

You will, of course, not have access to public IPv4 endpoints. You need to use providers and API that support IPv6, including AWS. For example, for AWS, you will need to use the dualstack endpoints that support IPv6.

wget -6 https://s3.dualstack.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/ec2-downloads-windows/SSMAgent/latest/debian_amd64/amazon-ssm-agent.deb

~/.aws/config (for root, ssm-user etc.)

[default]
use_dualstack_endpoint = true

/etc/amazon/ssm/amazon-ssm-agent.json

{
    "Agent": {
        "UseDualStackEndpoint": true
    }
}

Q: Error message: A fatal error occurred while creating a TLS client credential. The internal error state is 10013 A:
  1. Open Registry Editor, by “Run regedit”.
  2. Got to below directory  HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.0
  3. On the Client subfolder set the Enabled Data to 1, set the DisabledByDefault Data to 0.
  4. On the Server subfolder set the Enabled Data to 1, set the DisabledByDefault Data to 0.

Q: Exception occurred while the JNDI NamingManager was processing a javax.naming.Reference object A:

I was facing the same issue and here was my resolution I had wrongly spelled my jta data source in IBM Admin Console and was using a different name in my persistence xml so Websphere couldn't connect. Please check the Resources Tab in the Admin Console and validate your jta data source name as declared in persistence xml
